prompt: Which of the following is true of the CEOI but NOT of the CESI?
options: Its format is identical to that of the other publication
It is divided into 7 or 8 distinct sections
It is prepared in four editions
explanation: Page 11 says the CEOI is prepared in four editions while the CESI is prepared in only one. Both are combat orders with an identical format and 7 or 8 sections (pages 10 and 13).

prompt: The CEOI is prepared for short periods and is subject to frequent change, whereas the CESI is:
options: Numbered according to the CEOI items
explanation: Page 12 says the CESI is permanent in nature and that the specific items in the CEOI obtain their numbers from the CESI.

prompt: Both the CEOI and the CESI are divided into how many distinct sections?
explanation: Page 13 lists as a similarity that both the CEOI and the CESI are divided into 7 or 8 distinct sections.

prompt: Which statement about the signal officer's responsibility is correct?
options: He is responsible for preparing and issuing the CEOI only
He is responsible for communication at command level in place of the commander
He is responsible for authenticating every transmitted message
He is responsible for preparing and issuing both the CESI and the CEOI
explanation: Page 14 says the signal officer is responsible for the preparation and issuance of both the CESI and CEOI, while communication is the responsibility of the commander.

prompt: Which of the following is assigned to each published copy to facilitate distribution, control and accounting?
explanation: Page 15 says both the CESI and CEOI are assigned a copy number for each copy published.

prompt: The short title, a combination of characters or a pronounceable word, is assigned to provide:
options: A sequence for editions within a calendar year
explanation: Page 16 says the short title provides brevity and additional security measures and identifies a particular edition.

prompt: The 3rd edition of the CEOI is the second reserve. Where is it kept?
options: With the using unit, apart from the basic edition
In the storage vault of the preparing headquarters
At the command post as extracts
explanation: Page 23 says the 3rd edition, the second reserve, is prepared and published but not issued to the using unit and is kept in the issuing headquarters. The 4th edition is the one kept in the storage vault (page 24).

prompt: When a CEOI is compromised, it is immediately pulled out of circulation and the first reserve is upgraded into:
explanation: Page 26 says that in case of compromise, the document is immediately pulled out of circulation and the first reserve or second edition is upgraded into the first or basic edition.

prompt: Which pair of items indicates the units authorized to receive copies and the identity of each published copy?
explanation: Page 30 says the distribution item specifies the units to receive copies and how many, and page 15 says the copy number identifies each published copy for accounting. The short title identifies only an edition (page 16).

prompt: Which of the following is NOT a condition that makes a CEOI or CESI compromised?
options: It is replaced by the next edition on its effective date
It is misused so as to endanger the security of the communication-electronic system
explanation: Page 17 says compromise exists when the document is known or believed to have been captured, lost, exposed to unauthorized personnel or misused so as to endanger security. Routine replacement is not compromise.

prompt: The immediate report of a compromise is sent by the fastest means. The subsequent written report goes through:
options: Direct to the G6/S6 of the issuing headquarters
The using unit's signal officer only
explanation: Page 18 says the immediate report goes by the fastest means direct to the G6/S6 of the issuing headquarters, while the subsequent written report (investigation report) goes through command channels.

prompt: Which list contains the information added in the subsequent written report on a compromise?
options: Short title of the compromised edition; item numbers of compromised items; date and time of compromise
Circumstances leading to the compromise; person(s) responsible; action taken; recommendation to prevent similar occurrences
Circumstances leading to the compromise; short title of the compromised edition; date and time of compromise
Person(s) responsible; action taken; fastest means of transmission
explanation: Page 18 says the written report contains the information of the immediate report plus the circumstances, person(s) responsible, action taken and recommendations to prevent similar occurrences. The short title and date and time belong to the immediate report.

prompt: Which section occupies item numbers 20 through 29?
explanation: Page 33 gives the Authentication Section item numbers 20-29. The Messenger Section is 10-19 (page 32), Code and Cipher 30-49 (page 34) and Radio 50-59 (page 35).

prompt: Which statement about compromise of a CEOI or CESI is correct?
options: It includes a document believed to have been exposed to unauthorized personnel, not only one confirmed captured or lost
It applies only to a document confirmed to have been captured
It requires proof of misuse before it may be reported
It applies to the CEOI but not to the CESI
explanation: Page 17 defines compromise as a CEOI/CESI known or believed to have been captured, lost, exposed to unauthorized personnel or misused, so belief is enough and both publications are covered.

prompt: Which statement describes the Messenger Section?
options: It contains the various codes and ciphers used
It contains the telephone directory and wire tagging code
It contains email addresses and data encryption keys
It contains information on motor and air messenger schedules
explanation: Page 32 says the Messenger Section (items 10-19) contains information on motor and air messenger schedules. The others describe the Code and Cipher, Wire and Information System Sections.

prompt: In the Code and Cipher Section, the VIP code is a word of how many letters?
explanation: Page 34 gives the geographical code as a 5-6 letter word, the operation code as a 3 letter pronounceable word, the VIP code as a 5-9 letter word and the rest of the codes as 5-8 letter words.

prompt: General Information, a mandatory item of the General Section, must be made part of the:
explanation: Page 31 says general information must be made part of the command SOP and covers security, communication media, message preparation and other information the commander desires.

prompt: The edition number, which appears after the hyphen in an item number, is numbered consecutively within the:
explanation: Page 41 says the edition number appears after the hyphen and editions are numbered consecutively within the calendar year.

prompt: The number of the item is repeated at the bottom right portion of each page in order to facilitate:
options: Location of a particular CEOI/CESI item
explanation: Page 46 says the item number is repeated at the bottom right portion of each page to facilitate location of a particular CEOI/CESI item.

prompt: The authentication in the Index indicates that:
options: The order is valid and is issued by, or for, the commander
The copy is properly accounted for
The message came from a valid station
explanation: Page 47 says the entire CEOI/CESI is authenticated for the commander in the index to indicate that the order is valid and issued by, or for, the commander.
